mainTopic: Skins of the שרצים, the definition of חבורה, killing small creatures, and other שבת liabilities for harming living things
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing a ברייתא about which of the eight שרצים have a real skin. After אביי and רבא each offer a reading, רב אדא בר מתנה concludes that רבי יוחנן בן נורי and חכמים argue only about טומאה. רב אשי shows that חכמים agree with רבי יוחנן בן נורי about wounding on שבת, and the ברייתא's wording is corrected to match. לוי learns from the פסוק about a כושי's skin that a חבורה is a wound that does not go back. The גמרא then asks which תנא makes one liable for killing small creatures. רב יוסף explains that both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן learn from the rams of the משכן but stress different features, and he defends this against challenges about lice eggs and fleas. רב teaches, in three versions, that רבי שמעון exempts a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. Finally, שמואל rules on taking a fish out of water and on detaching a fetus, which רבא explains as עוקר דבר מגידולו, and אביי begins a statement that continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: Only Those the Sages Listed
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of a ברייתא that began on the previous עמוד, giving the view of חכמים against רבי יוחנן בן נורי about which שרצים have skin.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The Sages say: there is skin only] for those that the Sages enumerated.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last words of a ברייתא quoted on the previous עמוד. חכמים said that skin counts only for 'those that the Sages enumerated.' The גמרא is about to question this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that all eight שרצים have skins. חכמים limit this and point to a list. That list is the one in משנה חולין: the אנקה, כח, לטאה, and חומט, whose skin is treated like their flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: The eight creeping creatures listed in the תורה (ויקרא יא)
For those that the Sages enumerated (in a list)
Skin, meaning a skin that counts as separate from the flesh

phrases.english: for those that the Sages enumerated.
phrases.notes: The tail end of the ברייתא quoted at the bottom of 107a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted on the previous עמוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים say skin applies only to those creatures 'that the Sages enumerated.'

steps.title: The Opposite Is True: Those Listed Have No Separate Skin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the creatures the Sages listed are exactly the ones whose skin is NOT separate, because their skin is like their flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! Those that the Sages enumerated have no skin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording. The Sages' list is the list of creatures whose skin is considered flesh, so they are the ones WITHOUT a separate skin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In משנה חולין, the Sages listed four שרצים whose skin is treated like flesh. So saying 'only those listed have skin' seems to say the exact opposite of what that list means.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary; the reverse is true

phrases.english: On the contrary, those that the Sages enumerated
have no skin!
phrases.notes: Their skin is like their flesh (משנה חולין ט:ב).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'there is skin only for those the Sages enumerated.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Sages' list is the list of creatures whose skin equals flesh, so the ברייתא seems to say the reverse of the known law.

steps.title: אביי: It Means Those the Sages Did NOT List
steps.stepSummary: אביי reinterprets the ברייתא: only creatures NOT on the Sages' list have skin that is separate from the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: This is what it means: skin is separate from flesh only for those that the Sages did not enumerate.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the problem by reading the ברייתא as talking about the creatures NOT on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אביי's reading, the listed four have skin like flesh, and all the rest have a separate skin. This fits the law, but it requires reading 'did not enumerate' into words that say 'enumerated.'

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a reinterpretation)

phrases.english: And Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
skin is not separate from flesh
except for those that the Sages did not enumerate,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by reinterpreting the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say the listed ones have skin.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the unlisted ones have separate skin.

steps.title: רבא: But It Says 'Enumerated'
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's reading because the ברייתא clearly says 'those that the Sages enumerated,' not 'did not enumerate.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: But it says 'those that the Sages enumerated'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on אביי. His reading reverses the actual words of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A good explanation should fit the words we have. אביי's reading needs a 'not' that is not in the text, so רבא looks for a reading that keeps 'enumerated.'

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (a direct response)
But it says...! (pointing to the actual words)

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
But it says 'for those that the Sages enumerated'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts the plain words of the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבא: Only the Listed Ones' Skin Transmits טומאה Like Flesh
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the ברייתא as being about טומאה: only the skin of the listed creatures makes things impure like their flesh does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: This is what it means: skin does not transmit טומאה like flesh except for those the Sages enumerated.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own reading. It keeps the word 'enumerated' by making the ברייתא about טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'enumerated' fits perfectly. The listed four have skin that counts as flesh, so their skin is מטמא. 'Having skin' here means having skin that transmits טומאה like flesh.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said: This is what it is saying:
skin does not transmit impurity like flesh
except for those that the Sages enumerated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's reading with a new one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase seemed to be about having separate skin.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is about skin that transmits טומאה like flesh.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן בן נורי Make Unlisted Skins Impure?
steps.stepSummary: If חכמים say only the listed ones' skin is מטמא, then רבי יוחנן בן נורי seems to hold that even unlisted ones' skin is מטמא. But a ברייתא says he holds the eight have skins that are NOT מטמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: By implication, does רבי יוחנן בן נורי hold that even those the Sages did not list transmit טומאה? But it was taught: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the eight שרצים have skins and they do not transmit טומאה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's reading. It makes רבי יוחנן בן נורי look stricter than חכמים, but we know he is actually more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חכמים's 'only' limits טומאה to the listed four, the person arguing should hold that more skins are מטמא. But רבי יוחנן בן נורי says all eight have real skins that are NOT מטמא. So the argument is set up backwards.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught! (a contradiction from a source)
The תנא who holds all eight שרצים have skins

phrases.english: By implication, that Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri holds

phrases.aramaic: הָנָךְ נָמֵי דְּלֹא מָנוּ חֲכָמִים מְטַמְּאִין?
phrases.english: that even those that the Sages did not enumerate transmit impurity?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא קָתָנֵי, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But it is taught: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says:
the eight creeping animals have skins
and they do not transmit impurity!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's reading through what it implies.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes רבי יוחנן בן נורי stricter about טומאה, but a ברייתא shows he is more lenient.

steps.title: רב אדא בר מתנה: Regarding טומאה, the Listed Ones Have No Skin
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר מתנה rephrases חכמים: regarding טומאה, the listed creatures have no separate skin. So the argument with רבי יוחנן בן נורי is about טומאה only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר מתנה said: Explain it this way: And חכמים say: regarding טומאה, there is no skin for those the Sages enumerated.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר מתנה fixes the reading. חכמים are saying that for the listed four, the skin does not count as separate when it comes to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says all eight have real skin that is not מטמא. חכמים answer that for the listed four, the skin counts as flesh and is מטמא. The words 'regarding טומאה' limit the whole argument to טומאה.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אדא בר מתנה, רבי יוחנן בן נורי and חכמים argue only about טומאה. The listed four (אנקה, כח, לטאה, חומט) have skin that counts as flesh.

phrases.aramaic: [אָמַר רַב] אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה: תָּרֵיץ הָכִי,
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Mattana said: Resolve it this way:
And the Sages say:
with regard to impurity there is no skin
for those that the Sages enumerated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר מַתְנָה: תָּרֵיץ הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rephrasing the ברייתא and limiting its scope
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חכמים were limiting which skins are מטמא, which made רבי יוחנן בן נורי stricter.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים say the listed ones' skin is not separate regarding טומאה, and the argument is only about טומאה.

steps.title: But They Seem to Argue About שבת Too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about trapping and wounding שרצים on שבת. There, רבי יוחנן בן נורי seems to argue against a first opinion that limits liability to שרצים with skins.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, do they not argue regarding שבת? But it was taught: One who traps one of the eight שרצים in the תורה, or wounds them, is liable, for שרצים that have skins. What is a wound that does not go back? Blood gathered, even if it did not come out. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: the eight שרצים have skins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the argument is only about טומאה. A ברייתא about שבת shows the same argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says wounding makes one liable only for 'שרצים that have skins,' so it assumes some of the eight have none. רבי יוחנן בן נורי replies that all eight have skins. So there seems to be an argument about שבת as well.

keyTerms.meaning: One who traps (the מלאכה of צידה)
A wound that does not go back (is permanent)

steps.confusionAlert: A חבורה here does not require bleeding out. Blood that gathers under the skin, like a bruise, is enough.

phrases.english: But still, with regard to Shabbat do they not disagree?
But it was taught: One who traps one
of the eight creeping animals mentioned in the Torah,
one who wounds them is liable,
with creeping animals that have skins.
And what is a wound that does not go back?

phrases.aramaic: נִצְרַר הַדָּם אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא יָצָא.
phrases.english: The blood gathered, even though it did not come out.
Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri says:
the eight creeping animals have skins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion that the argument is only about טומאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר מתנה's limitation of the argument to טומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא shows רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagreeing with a first opinion on a שבת law.

steps.title: רב אשי: The First Opinion Is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the first opinion in the שבת ברייתא is רבי יהודה, who judges skin by its texture. חכמים, who argue with רבי יוחנן בן נורי about טומאה, agree with him about שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Who is the first תנא? רבי יהודה, who goes by the texture. As we learned: רבי יהודה says the לטאה is like the חולדה. But the רבנן who argue with רבי יוחנן about טומאה agree with him about שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by naming the first opinion. It is רבי יהודה, not חכמים, so חכמים still agree about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה judges by how thick the skin feels, so he counts the לטאה as having real skin like the חולדה. That is why he says only some שרצים 'have skins.' חכמים's argument with רבי יוחנן בן נורי stays limited to טומאה, and for wounding on שבת they agree all eight have skin.

keyTerms.meaning: The lizard is like the weasel

steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the rule that a חבורה on שבת applies to all eight שרצים according to חכמים, while their argument about טומאה stays separate.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאן תַּנָּא קַמָּא —
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: Who is the first tanna?
Rabbi Yehuda, who goes after the texture.
As we learned in a mishna: Rabbi Yehuda says:
The lizard is like the weasel.
But the Rabbis, who disagree with
Rabbi Yoḥanan with regard to impurity,
with regard to Shabbat agree with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מַאן תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שבת challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first opinion in the שבת ברייתא was חכמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is רבי יהודה. חכמים agree with רבי יוחנן בן נורי about שבת.

steps.title: Then the ברייתא Should Mention His Opponents Too
steps.stepSummary: If חכמים agree with רבי יוחנן בן נורי about שבת, the ברייתא should say 'the words of רבי יוחנן בן נורי and his opponents,' not just his words.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this phrase 'the words of רבי יוחנן בן נורי' should have been 'the words of רבי יוחנן and his opponents'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's answer from the wording of the ברייתא. It credits the view only to רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חכמים also hold that all eight have skin for שבת, the view is not his alone. The ברייתא should show that his usual opponents share it here.

keyTerms.meaning: And those who disagree with him

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, הַאי ״דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי״,
phrases.english: If so, this 'the words of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri',
it should have said 'the words of Rabbi Yoḥanan and those who disagree with him'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that חכמים agree about שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא gives the view to רבי יוחנן בן נורי alone.

steps.title: Correct the Text: Add 'and His Opponents'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the ברייתא to read 'the words of רבי יוחנן בן נורי and his opponents.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it: 'the words of רבי יוחנן בן נורי and his opponents.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by correcting the wording of the ברייתא so it fits רב אשי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of giving up רב אשי's answer, the גמרא fixes the text. This confirms that for שבת, רבי יוחנן בן נורי and חכמים agree that all eight שרצים have skins.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it as; emend the text to read

steps.whatToRemember: For שבת, all agree except רבי יהודה that all eight שרצים have skins, so wounding any of them makes one liable. The argument between רבי יוחנן בן נורי and חכמים is only about טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנִי: ״דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי וּמַחְלוּקְתּוֹ״.
phrases.english: Teach: 'the words of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri and those who disagree with him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the wording challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא credited the view to רבי יוחנן בן נורי alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The text is corrected to include his opponents.

steps.title: לוי Asks: What Is the Source for a Permanent Wound?
steps.stepSummary: לוי asks רבי for the source that a חבורה is defined as a wound that does not go back.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי asked רבי: From where do we know that a חבורה is one that does not go back?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. לוי asks for the source behind the definition of a חבורה used in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא defined a חבורה as a wound that does not go back. לוי wants to know where in the פסוקים this definition comes from.

phrases.english: Levi asked of Rabbi:
From where do we know that a wound is one that does not go back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about the definition of חבורה mentioned in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a חבורה is a permanent wound.

steps.title: The Verse: Can a Cushite Change His Skin?
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers with the פסוק in ירמיה: 'Can a כושי change his skin, or a leopard its חברבורות?'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Can a כושי change his skin, or a leopard its spots?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a פסוק as the source. The next steps explain how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'חברבורותיו,' which sounds like 'חבורה.' The פסוק pairs it with a כושי's skin, which never changes.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Can a Cushite change his skin,
or a leopard its spots?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers לוי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'הֲיַהֲפוֹךְ כּוּשִׁי עוֹרוֹ וְנָמֵר חֲבַרְבֻּרֹתָיו.'

steps.title: What Does 'חברבורותיו' Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word 'חברבורותיו' means. This sets up how the פסוק proves the point.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'חברבורותיו'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup question. The גמרא wants to pin down the meaning of the key word before drawing the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if 'חברבורותיו' means wounds. The גמרא will test the other possible meaning first.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean?

phrases.english: What is 'ḥavarburotav'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up the explanation of the פסוק.

steps.title: It Cannot Mean Colored Spots
steps.stepSummary: If 'חברבורותיו' meant colored spots, the פסוק should have said 'its colors.' So that reading is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means spotted patterns, then 'or a leopard its חברבורות' should have said 'or a leopard its colors'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the simple meaning, colored spots, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק meant colors, it would have used the plain word for colors. Using 'חברבורות' instead points to a different meaning: wounds.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say that it means it stands in spotted patterns,
this 'or a leopard its spots',
it should have said 'a leopard its colors'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects one meaning of the word.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of 'חברבורותיו' as colored spots
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק would have simply said 'גווניו' (its colors).

steps.title: Like a Cushite's Skin, a Wound Does Not Go Back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'חברבורותיו' means wounds, which are compared to a כושי's skin: just as his skin never changes, a חבורה does not go back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like the כושי: just as the skin of a כושי does not change back, so too a חבורה does not go back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. A חבורה is defined as a permanent mark, compared to the unchanging skin of a כושי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places 'חברבורות' next to a כושי's skin, so they share the same feature. They are permanent. This is the source for defining a חבורה on שבת as a wound that does not go back.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not go back; is permanent

steps.whatToRemember: A חבורה on שבת is a wound that does not go back, such as blood gathering under the skin. The source is the פסוק comparing 'חברבורות' to a כושי's unchanging skin.

phrases.english: Rather, it is like the Cushite:
just as the skin of a Cushite does not change back,
so too a wound does not go back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct meaning after rejecting the first one, and completes the answer to לוי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A חבורה is a permanent wound, learned from the פסוק comparing it to a כושי's unchanging skin.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה and inferring that killing other creatures is liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about other שקצים and infers that killing them makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And other שקצים' (one who wounds them is exempt). This implies that if one kills them, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה and draws an inference from it. This sets up the next question: who holds this view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that wounding other שקצים is exempt. The גמרא reads this to mean that killing them is liable. That inference is the claim the גמרא now needs to attribute to a specific תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Small creatures such as bugs and crawling things (not the eight שרצים listed in the תורה)

phrases.english: 'And other abominations, etc.'
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה, which says one who wounds them is exempt.

phrases.english: This implies: if one kills them, he is liable.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is reading this out of how the משנה is worded.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁאָר שְׁקָצִים כּוּ׳. הָא הוֹרְגָן חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the next clause of the משנה after finishing the discussion of what a חבורה is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wounding other שקצים is exempt, which implies that killing them is liable.

steps.title: Which תנא holds this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that killing other שקצים makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion this inference follows. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone agrees that killing tiny creatures counts as the מלאכה of killing. So the גמרא wants to know which view the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Which תנא (author of the teaching) is this?

phrases.english: Who is the Tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the inference made in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that killing other שקצים is liable.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה says it is רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who compares killing a כינה to killing a camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: It is רבי אליעזר. A ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר says: One who kills a louse on שבת is like one who kills a camel on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers that the משנה follows רבי אליעזר. He brings a ברייתא to show that רבי אליעזר holds a person is liable for killing even the smallest creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If killing a tiny louse is like killing a camel, then killing any small creature is liable for רבי אליעזר. That matches the inference from the משנה. The hidden assumption is that the רבנן disagree and would not make one liable.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
It is Rabbi Eliezer.
As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who kills a louse on Shabbat
is like one who kills a camel on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who makes one liable for killing even a louse.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the רבנן agree for creatures that reproduce
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects that the רבנן argue only about lice, which do not reproduce. For other creatures they agree with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: The רבנן argue with רבי אליעזר only about lice, which do not reproduce. But about other שקצים and crawling creatures, which do reproduce, they do not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges the claim that the משנה follows only רבי אליעזר. He says the רבנן also agree in the משנה's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument in the ברייתא was only about a louse, which (they assumed) does not reproduce. The שקצים in the משנה do reproduce, so even the רבנן would make one liable for killing them. So there is no need to say the משנה follows only רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: They argue only up to this point (and not beyond)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objected to this:
The Rabbis disagree only
with Rabbi Eliezer regarding a louse,
which does not reproduce.
But other abominations and crawling creatures
which do reproduce, they do not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי ירמיה's attribution in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's claim that the משנה follows only רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן's disagreement is limited to non-reproducing lice. The משנה's שקצים reproduce, so everyone agrees killing them is liable.

steps.title: Both sides learn from the rams of the משכן
steps.stepSummary: Both רבי אליעזר and the רבנן learn the מלאכה of killing from the rams in the משכן. Each focuses on a different feature of the rams.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them learned it only from the rams. רבי אליעזר holds: just as rams have their life taken, so too anything whose life is taken counts. The רבנן hold: just as rams reproduce, so too anything that reproduces counts.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues רב יוסף's point by explaining where each side's view comes from. It shows why the רבנן draw the line at creatures that reproduce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מלאכה of killing is learned from the rams whose skins were used in the משכן. רבי אליעזר says the key feature is that the rams were alive and were killed, so any living thing counts, even a louse. The רבנן say the key feature is that rams reproduce, so only reproducing creatures count, and a louse is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rams (whose skins were used in the משכן)

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides learn from the rams. רבי אליעזר: any living thing counts. רבנן: only creatures that reproduce count.

phrases.english: And both of them learned it only from the rams.
Rabbi Eliezer holds: like rams —

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֵילִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה —
phrases.english: just as rams have their life taken,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נְטִילַת נְשָׁמָה.
phrases.english: so too anything whose life can be taken.
And the Rabbis hold: like rams —
just as rams reproduce,
so too anything that reproduces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source-based reasoning behind רב יוסף's distinction in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלאכה of killing comes from the rams. רבי אליעזר stresses taking life, and the רבנן stress reproduction.

steps.title: אביי: don't lice reproduce from eggs?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף from a saying that ה׳ feeds creatures down to 'lice eggs,' which suggests that lice reproduce.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do lice really not reproduce? But the Master said: The Holy One, Blessed be He, sits and feeds everything, from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's assumption that lice do not reproduce. He quotes a saying that mentions lice eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If lice lay eggs, then they do reproduce. Then even the רבנן should make one liable for killing them, and רב יוסף's explanation of the argument falls apart.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And a louse does not reproduce?
But didn't the Master say:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, sits and feeds
from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְכִינָּה אֵין פָּרָה וְרָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the factual premise of רב יוסף's position.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's premise that lice do not reproduce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A saying mentions 'lice eggs,' so lice seem to reproduce.

steps.title: 'Lice eggs' is the name of a different species
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that 'lice eggs' is the name of a separate species, not actual eggs of lice.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a species that is called 'lice eggs.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי by explaining that 'lice eggs' is just the name of a different kind of creature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying is not talking about eggs that lice lay. It refers to a separate creature with that name. So lice still do not reproduce, and רב יוסף's view stands.
steps.confusionAlert: 'ביצי כינים' here is a name for a creature. It does not mean real eggs laid by lice.

phrases.english: It is a species that is called 'lice eggs.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Lice eggs' means real eggs laid by lice, so lice reproduce.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Lice eggs' is the name of a separate species. Lice themselves do not reproduce.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists 'טפויין and lice eggs'
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא lists 'טפויין and lice eggs,' which again seems to show that lice lay eggs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: 'טפויין and lice eggs'!
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge to רב יוסף continues with a second source that mentions lice eggs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא lists 'lice eggs' among creatures. Again, that suggests lice reproduce.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught:
'Tefuyin and lice eggs'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge on the same point after the answer in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's premise that lice do not reproduce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא names 'lice eggs' in a list of creatures, which implies that lice lay eggs.

steps.title: Same answer: it is a separate species
steps.stepSummary: The same answer is given: 'lice eggs' in the ברייתא is the name of a separate species.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a species that is called 'lice eggs.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer to the second source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is also listing a creature named 'lice eggs.' It is not describing real eggs of lice, so lice still do not reproduce.

phrases.english: It is a species that is called 'lice eggs.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 the same way step 23 answered step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves that lice lay eggs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא names a separate species called 'lice eggs.'

steps.title: The flea reproduces, yet רבי יהושע exempts
steps.stepSummary: A flea reproduces, yet a ברייתא says רבי יהושע exempts one who catches a flea. That seems to argue against רב יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is a flea, which reproduces, and a ברייתא teaches: One who traps a flea on שבת, רבי אליעזר holds him liable and רבי יהושע exempts him!
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to רב יוסף comes from a ברייתא about a flea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A flea reproduces, so according to רב יוסף everyone should agree that it counts. Yet רבי יהושע exempts. That suggests the argument is not about reproduction at all.

phrases.english: But there is a flea, which reproduces,
and it was taught: One who traps a flea on Shabbat —
Rabbi Eliezer holds him liable
and Rabbi Yehoshua exempts him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to רב יוסף after the lice-egg challenges were answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that everyone agrees about creatures that reproduce.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A flea reproduces, yet רבי יהושע exempts, so the argument does not depend on reproduction.

steps.title: רב אשי: that argument is about trapping, not killing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the flea argument is about trapping a creature that is not normally trapped. For killing, even רבי יהושע agrees one is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Are you throwing trapping against killing? רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue only about this: one holds that trapping a kind of creature that is not normally trapped is liable, and the other holds it is exempt. But about killing, even רבי יהושע agrees.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the flea challenge. He shows that it mixes up two different מלאכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The flea argument is about trapping. Fleas are not a species people normally trap, and the argument is whether such trapping counts. It says nothing about killing, and for killing a flea even רבי יהושע agrees one is liable, so רב יוסף's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: You are throwing (one against the other)
A thing whose species is not normally trapped

steps.whatToRemember: The flea argument is only about trapping a creature not usually trapped. For killing, everyone agrees that a reproducing creature counts.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Are you throwing trapping against killing?!

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua disagree only
in that one Master holds:
a thing whose species is not usually trapped, one is liable,
and the other Master holds: exempt.
But regarding killing,
even Rabbi Yehoshua agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: צֵידָה אַהֲרִיגָה קָרָמֵית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the flea challenge of step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהושע exempts for a flea, so he does not count reproducing creatures for killing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Their argument is only about trapping a species not usually trapped. For killing, everyone agrees one is liable.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: trapping for a need is liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה: one who traps them for a need is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One who traps them for a need is liable, etc. (and not for a need is exempt).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. This sets up a question about who holds this view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates trapping that serves a purpose, which is liable, from trapping that serves no purpose, which is exempt. The גמרא now wants to know whose view this distinction follows.

keyTerms.meaning: For a need, for a purpose

phrases.english: 'One who traps them for a need is liable, etc.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trapping other שקצים for a need is liable, and without a need it is exempt.

steps.title: Which תנא holds this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא exempts trapping that is not done for a need.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose view this clause follows. It is setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Exempting trapping that is done without a need depends on a known argument between the תנאים. So the גמרא identifies the author.

phrases.english: Who is the Tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the clause quoted in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who exempts trapping that is not done for a need.

steps.title: It is רבי שמעון: a מלאכה not needed for itself is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says it is רבי שמעון, who exempts מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It is רבי שמעון, who said that for a מלאכה that is not needed for its own purpose, one is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון holds that a מלאכה done without its usual purpose is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trapping without a need is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה: the act happens, but the person does not want the result the מלאכה is normally done for. רבי שמעון exempts this kind of act, so he must be the author of the clause.

keyTerms.meaning: A מלאכה done without wanting its normal purpose

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'trapping for a need is liable, without a need is exempt' follows רבי שמעון's principle of מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.whyThisMatters: מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה is a major principle in הלכות שבת that comes up across the whole מסכת.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is Rabbi Shimon,
who said: a labor that is not needed for its own sake,
one is exempt for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause follows רבי שמעון, who exempts מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.

steps.title: Another version: the abscess case
steps.stepSummary: Some place רב's statement on a different ruling. That ruling says draining an abscess to make an opening makes one liable, but draining it only to let out pus is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach it on this: One who drains an abscess on שבת: if he does it to make an opening for it, he is liable. If he does it to let fluid out of it, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of which ruling רב's statement was attached to. This step sets up the 'which תנא?' question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the ruling being explained is about a מורסא (abscess), not about trapping. Making a real opening counts as a full מלאכה. Opening it only to drain out pus does not need the opening for its own sake, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it (this statement) on this other source

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on this:
One who drains an abscess on Shabbat,
if to make an opening for it, he is liable;
if to remove fluid from it, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source as the place where רב's statement from Step 30 was taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Draining an abscess to make an opening makes one liable. Draining it only to let out pus is exempt.

steps.title: Who holds the abscess ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא exempts draining an abscess just to let out pus.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whose opinion the abscess ruling follows. This sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption needs a source, because a person did make an opening. The גמרא wants to know which view allows exempting an act that technically matches a מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (which sage's view is this)?

phrases.english: Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the ruling quoted in Step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא exempts draining an abscess when it is not done to make an opening?

steps.title: רב: it is רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב says the abscess ruling follows רבי שמעון, who exempts מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It is רבי שמעון, who said that one is exempt for a מלאכה that is not needed for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers that the abscess ruling follows רבי שמעון. This is the same answer he gave in Step 30, now placed on a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone drains pus, he does not want the opening itself; he only wants the pus out. According to רבי שמעון, a מלאכה done without wanting its actual purpose is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A forbidden act done without needing its own purpose or result

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵין צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ — פָּטוּר עָלֶיהָ.
phrases.english: who said that for a labor not needed for its own sake, one is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling follows רבי שמעון's exemption for מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.

steps.title: A third version: the snake case
steps.stepSummary: Another version places רב's statement on a ruling about trapping a snake. Trapping it so it won't bite is exempt; trapping it for medicine makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some teach it on this: One who traps a snake on שבת: if he busies himself with it so that it won't bite him, he is exempt. If he does it for medicine, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives yet another version of where רב's statement belongs, this time a case of trapping a snake. This step sets up the same question and answer again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he traps the snake for medicine, he wants the snake itself, so this is real צידה (trapping). When he traps it only to protect himself, he does not need the trapped snake, so the act is not needed for its own sake.

keyTerms.meaning: Deals with it so it will not bite him

phrases.english: And there are those who teach it on this:
One who traps a snake on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אִם מִתְעַסֵּק בּוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יִשְּׁכֶנּוּ — פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: if he deals with it so that it will not bite him, he is exempt;
if for medicine, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third possible source for רב's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trapping a snake for self-protection is exempt. Trapping it for medicinal use makes one liable.

steps.title: Who holds the snake ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא exempts trapping a snake for protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who holds this?
steps.whatsHappening: The same question is asked about the snake case. This sets up רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act still looks like trapping, so the exemption needs a source in some תנא's view.

phrases.english: Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the author of the ruling in Step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא exempts trapping a snake when it is done only to avoid being bitten?

steps.title: Again: it is רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב attributes the snake ruling to רבי שמעון's exemption for מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: It is רבי שמעון, who said that one is exempt for a מלאכה that is not needed for its own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the same answer: the snake ruling follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three versions (Steps 30, 33, 36) share one idea. They disagree only about which case רב was explaining. The principle is always רבי שמעון's מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.whatToRemember: Whichever version you follow (trapping for no need, draining an abscess, or trapping a snake), רב always explains the exemption through רבי שמעון's rule of מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
It is Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מְלָאכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה לְגוּפָהּ פָּטוּר עָלֶיהָ.
phrases.english: who said that for a labor not needed for its own sake, one is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The snake ruling follows רבי שמעון.

steps.title: Taking a fish out of the sea
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that one who takes a fish out of the sea is liable once a סלע-sized area on it has dried.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: One who takes a fish out of the sea is liable once an area the size of a סלע coin on it has dried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: when taking a fish out of water counts as killing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once that much of the fish has dried, it can no longer survive. So the person is liable for נטילת נשמה (taking a life), even though the fish is still moving.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulls a fish out of the water
The size of a סלע coin
Taking a life (the מלאכה of killing)

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One who takes a fish out of the sea,
once an area the size of a sela has dried on it, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַשּׁוֹלֶה דָּג מִן הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to killing creatures on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking a fish out of water makes one liable once a סלע-sized area on it has dried.

steps.title: The dry spot is between the fins
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין says the dry area that counts is the area between the fins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: And between its fins.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין adds a detail about where on the fish the drying has to happen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר אבין narrows שמואל's rule. The סלע-sized dry area counts only when it is between the fins, because drying there is what decides whether the fish can still live.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
And between its fins.
phrases.notes: Read this as: the drying counts when it's in the area between the fins.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין: וּבֵין סְנַפִּירָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies where the drying in Step 37 must take place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The relevant dry area is between the fins.

steps.title: Sticky mucus counts as dry
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the fish does not need to be fully dry. Even sticky mucus forming on it is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Do not say it must be truly dry. Rather, even if it has formed sticky threads, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains what 'dried' means in שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liability starts earlier than a beginner might think. Once the skin turns sticky and forms strands, the fish has already reached the point where it cannot live.
steps.whatToRemember: For the fish, liability begins when a סלע-sized area between the fins has dried. Even a sticky, mucus-like stage counts as dry.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Do not say actually dry,
rather, even if it formed sticky strands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לָא תֵּימָא יָבֵשׁ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Further defines 'dried' in שמואל's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the sticky, mucus-forming stage counts as 'dried' for liability.

steps.title: Detaching a fetus inside an animal
steps.stepSummary: מר בר המדורי quotes שמואל: one who reaches into an animal and detaches the fetus inside it is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר המדורי said in the name of שמואל: One who reached his hand into an animal's womb and detached the fetus inside it is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling of שמואל is brought. Its reason is not given yet, and the next step will ask for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is surprising that this is a forbidden מלאכה, because the fetus is not killed in an ordinary way and is not a separate creature. That surprise is what sets up the question 'why?'.

keyTerms.meaning: The innards or womb of an animal

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר בַּר הַמְדּוּרֵי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Mar bar Hamdurei said that Shmuel said:
One who reached his hand into the innards of an animal
and detached the fetus in its womb is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר הַמְדּוּרֵי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts another ruling of שמואל about harming living things on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Detaching a fetus inside an animal makes one liable.

steps.title: Why is he liable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the fetus ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which מלאכה this act falls under. This sets up רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No obvious מלאכה fits. It is not clearly killing and not clearly trapping, so the גמרא needs to name the category.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind Step 40.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which category of מלאכה makes detaching a fetus a liable act?

steps.title: Uprooting from its place of growth
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains, as he heard from בר המדורי, that the fetus is like hops pulled off thorns. Both count as עוקר דבר מגידולו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: בר המדורי explained it to me. Didn't רב ששת say that one who pulls hops off shrubs and thorns is liable for uprooting a thing from where it grows? Here too, he is liable for uprooting a thing from where it grows.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by comparing the fetus to a plant being uprooted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hops that grow on thorns are not growing in the ground, yet pulling them off still counts as uprooting from their source of growth. In the same way, a fetus grows from its mother, so detaching it is עוקר דבר מגידולו (a form of קוצר, harvesting).

keyTerms.meaning: Uprooting something from where it grows

steps.confusionAlert: The liability here is not for killing the fetus. It is for uprooting something from the source it grows from, which is a form of harvesting.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that 'uprooting from growth' is not limited to plants in the ground. It applies to anything that draws its growth from a source.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Bar Hamdurei explained it to me:
Didn't Rav Sheshet say:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי מַאן דִּתְלַשׁ כְּשׁוּתָא מֵהִיזְמֵי וְהִיגֵי
phrases.english: One who detaches hops from shrubs and thorns
is liable for uprooting a thing from its place of growth.
Here too,
he is liable for uprooting a thing from its place of growth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: בַּר הַמְדּוּרֵי אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 41 by comparing the case to רב ששת's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Detaching the fetus counts as עוקר דבר מגידולו, just like pulling hops off thorns.

steps.title: אביי begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts a ruling about someone who detaches something. The statement continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: One who detaches…
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line: אביי begins a new statement that finishes on the next עמוד. It is preparing the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'one who detaches' suggests אביי will build on the idea of עוקר דבר מגידולו. The full ruling comes on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
One who detaches
phrases.notes: Statement continues on the next עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a further ruling about detaching, continuing from Step 42.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incomplete on this עמוד; it concerns liability for detaching something.
